r.t: Total seats across all 3 screens. ConnPlex Signature format = up to 175-260 seats across 3 screens (source: ConnPlex franchise disclosure). Mix: 80 Sofa Sliders + 50 Recliners + 70 Duo Loungers (see Investment tab).
5 shows/day is standard for Indian multiplexes.
18 weekday + 12 weekend days = 30-day month approximation.

Conservative base-case weekday occupancy. PVR INOX's company-wide (all-screen, all-day) average occupancy is ~22-24% (Source: ICICI Direct/Sharekhan, FY26). A new single-location premium cinema is modelled below the chain average on weekdays.

Weekday ATP. PVR INOX national blended ATP = Rs.259-262 (FY25-Q2 FY26, Source: Business Standard/ICICI Direct). This model prices a weekday luxury-recliner seat below that national blend to stay accessible; weekend ATP carries the premium instead.

Weekend/holiday occupancy. ConnPlex's own franchise disclosure claims '60%+ industry-leading occupancy' (source: franchiseavs.com). This model uses 55% weekend occupancy as a prudent haircut to that brand claim for institutional underwriting - see the Dashboard tab for an upside sensitivity at the brand's own 60%+ claim.

Weekend/holiday ATP - luxury recliner premium. PVR INOX has stated select premium/recliner screens price Rs.600-700 (Source: aparnadecors.com, citing MD Ajay Bijli); Rs.320 is a moderate premium versus the Rs.259-262 national blended ATP, appropriate for Ahmedabad's price-sensitive-but-growing market.
Blended occupancy = total tickets sold / total seat-shows available (weighted average, not a simple mean).

GST on cinema tickets priced above Rs.100 remains 18% under the GST 2.0 reform effective 22-Sep-2025 (tickets <=Rs.100 were cut from 12% to 5%). Source: GST Council 56th meeting; The Hans India / Vakilsearch, Sep 2025.

Industry-standard nett split: distributor/producer takes ~50% of net box office in week 1, declining to ~42.5% (wk2), 37.5% (wk3), 30% (wk4+) as exhibitor share rises (Source: Koimoi/IndiaForums trade analysis). This model conservatively holds the highest (week-1) 50% rate for every show, understating exhibitor profit for prudent underwriting.

Franchisee retains 80% of net ticket share; 20% is the ConnPlex brand royalty/franchise fee - within the typical 10-20% royalty band seen across Indian retail & F&B franchise agreements. Edit if your signed franchise agreement specifies a different royalty rate.
Optional ancillary revenue: private hall bookings / corporate screenings. Defaults to 0; raise this if the franchisee plans to sell private screenings.
Illustrative rate: Rs.99 x total seats, as in the original franchise model.
Ad spots/brand tie-ups sold per month across 3 screens + lobby/foyer branding.

Rate per spot/month. PVR INOX's ad income is ~6-8% of total revenue at scale (Q2 FY26 ad income Rs.125.6cr vs total revenue Rs.1,858.9cr = 6.8%, Source: Business Standard). This is a sanity-check ratio, not a per-spot benchmark - single-location boutique cinemas typically sell local/regional ad inventory directly.
Footfall = monthly tickets sold (concession spend is modelled per attendee, i.e. Spend-Per-Head).

F&B Spend-Per-Head (SPH). PVR INOX's national SPH reached an all-time high of Rs.148 in Q1 FY26 (Source: ICICI Direct); FY25 average was Rs.134 (Source: Digital Cinema Report). Rs.180 reflects a premium-format uplift consistent with a 100%-recliner luxury cinema.
Commission paid to the ad-sales agency for sourcing brand tie-ups.

Under GST 2.0 (effective 22-Sep-2025), F&B sold in cinemas as a stand-alone 'restaurant service' (not bundled with the ticket) attracts 5% GST - down from 18% pre-reform for combo/bundled sales (Source: Business Standard; GST Council 50th & 56th meetings). If F&B is sold bundled with tickets it reverts to the 18% ticket rate - keep concessions billed separately to retain this saving.
Backs the GST component out of a GST-inclusive concession price.
Franchisee retains 80% of gross ad revenue; 20% brand royalty, consistent with the ticket & F&B royalty split.
Food/beverage cost-of-goods ratio. Cinema concessions typically run 70-75% gross margin (25-30% COGS) industry-wide.
Franchisee retains 80% of net F&B revenue (20% brand royalty), matching the ticket-income split.
ConnPlex Signature format.

Ahmedabad CG Road high-street retail rents run Rs.120-300/sq.ft/month (Source: thesimplebizman.com, 2024-25). A cinema anchor tenant on a ~6,900-7,500 sq.ft footprint typically negotiates well below high-street rates; Rs.500,000/mo implies ~Rs.65-70/sq.ft - consistent with typical mall-anchor cinema deals.
Common Area Maintenance. Mall CAM charges typically run Rs.10-15/sq.ft/month on top of base rent.
Broadband, POS, ticketing & digital signage connectivity for a 3-screen site.
3-screen luxury multiplex with full HVAC + laser projection is power-intensive; Gujarat commercial tariffs run ~Rs.7-8/unit.
Annual maintenance contracts for projection, sound, seating & HVAC systems.
Fire, property & public-liability cover for a public entertainment venue.
Conservative like-for-like growth from occupancy ramp-up & ATP inflation as the property matures (typical multiplex maturity curve). Edit to stress-test.
Stationery, licenses renewal, housekeeping consumables, contingency.
Two trained projectionists across 3 screens.
Box-office and concession-counter staff - scaled for a 200-seat, 3-screen premium format.
Auditorium & lobby housekeeping team.
24x7 security personnel.
2% of monthly ticket + F&B income - a typical retail/entertainment marketing budget ratio. This is formula-linked so it auto-scales with revenue.
